candidates.title: Tried running it on version koboldcpp-1.114.1 with low ram
candidates.body:
**Hardware:**
Motherboard: LGA 1200. Chipset: H510. CPU: Pentium (2 cores, 4 threads).
RAM: 4 GB DDR4.
Video Card: Tesla P40 (24 GB VRAM), 2 cards. 24 x 2 VRAM = 48 GB VRAM.
OS: Windows 10 Ent (latest service pack)

**Additional Information:**
 I tried running it on version koboldcpp-1.114.1, model qwen3.6-27B.
I tried using CUDA and Vulkan, but neither option allowed the video card to run the model.
koboldcpp-1.114.1 crashes when loading the model, displaying something like a memory allocation error in the console.
I notice that the number of allocated bytes in the console error when the program crashes is approximately equal to the size of the model on the disk!
Got it!

Let's try to fix it:
Create a swap partition on the SSD. Then enable the "mlock" option in koboldcpp to prevent data from being loaded into memory.

"It works, but it's broken," and only on the koboldcpp-oldpc.exe version. Run it via the Vulkan API.
The funny thing is, the graphics card isn't loaded, and the graphics card's memory is completely empty... but it works, as far as I understand, all the calculations are done on the CPU.

Let's try to fix it:
Change several parameters and get an error about not being able to allocate 1 GB of memory for some Vulkan buffer. I notice that the ZGPU program sees Vulkan, but not its version? That's strange, I think the version on this driver should be 1.3.
Great, then let's try running it via CUDA.

ZGPU detects the CUDA version (I think it's the framework version, driver version 12.2, and the hardware version for the P40 card is 6.0). It crashes when running koboldcpp.exe and koboldcpp-oldpc.exe.

Another funny thing was that the card's OpenGL version was 1.1, although it should have been 4.6, I think, but I fixed that. OpenGL appeared when turning on the virtual screen.

I thought there might be a driver issue. I tried 9 different drivers, all of which gave similar results (it doesn't work).

1) Is it possible to run such a neural network using only the video card's VRAM for storing weights and 4 GB of RAM + SAWP SSD 32 GB? So, should the VRAM be loaded into the card's memory in chunks?

2) Koboldcpp.exe version 1.114.1 doesn't work on the CPU (without graphics cards), and koboldcpp-oldpc.exe automatically sets "Very Old CPU FailSafe" when loading from a file and only works in that file... Is a Pentium on LGA1200 an old processor, considering its 2020 technology? Why then does koboldcpp.exe work in simple CPU mode on my second motherboard with a Xeon E7-88XXv4 from 2016?

3) Is there any way to check the problem? I've spent 30 hours and still can't get it to work, tried different gguf models. I think there could be more than one issue, for example, the fact that the processor is a Pentium (even though it's new and supports AVX and AVX2), the CUDA driver version doesn't match the library version in the koboldcpp software, there's not enough RAM.

4) Is it possible to run through Vulkan with full loading of the neural network and KV cache into the card memory?

5) Is it possible to run through CUDA with full loading of the neural network and KV cache into the card memory?

6) Which should be upgraded first, the processor or the RAM?

candidates.body:
**Describe the Issue**
I'm using kobold to generate images, and I'm trying to build a node based UI, something like ComfyUI.

So my plan is to chain `/sdapi/v1/img2img` calls with nodes and queues, but between those calls also call Kobold admin API, to switch configs/models.

By posting to `/api/admin/reload_config` for example `{"filename": "model.gguf", "overrideconfig": "config.kcpps}`

The **issue** is that the admin api returns response immediatley, that hey request was successful, but in reality the model switch is still in progress.

Could this be changed, so **reload_config** would return promise that resolves, once Kobold is ready to be prompted again.

candidates.title: Enhancement: dedicated context cache per-client
candidates.body:
Once again an attempt to formalize how a permanent context caching could be done in koboldcpp.

Flow:

1. Server option "cache history context on disk", accepts a path string to a directory. When not empty, the feature is enabled and koboldcpp exposes cache list field in API for Lite (an array of strings). The first one is always present and named "(default)".
2. Lite receives cache list field during initial fetching. If present, Lite would know that cache is enabled for this koboldcpp instance.
3. In this case, Lite shows a special dropdown/select inside "Save/Load" popup, named "Context cache file" with a list of strings that came from the server, and another option named "<add new cache file>".
4. User may select any item, initially the first one "(default)" should be selected. This key (let's call it "context_cache_file") is sent to the server for each generation request.
5. If the user selects the last one "<add new cache file>", a text field becomes visible where a custom new name can be entered instead.
6. When koboldcpp with enabled context caching receives a new generation request, it reads the "context_cache_file" key that Lite sent. If there was no such key or it is empty, the value "(default)" is used.
7. If this context cache name was not known to the server before, the context cache list is updated, adding this value to the end.
8. When sending generation results back to client, koboldcpp adds a full context cache list each time.
9. When Lite receives a generation result, it updates "Context cache file" dropdown with values from this list; if a text field with a custom name was not empty, and the value equals to one entry from the list – the current dropdown/select chooses it, hiding the field; if for some reason the current name is no longer in the list (maybe koboldcpp was restarted with different settings) – selection drops to "(default)"; if there is no list at all, the dropdown should be hidden completely, since the restarted server does not support it anymore.

Main work:
1. Assume koboldcpp server can save and load history contexts (KV cache &co) in files by means of llama.cpp.
2. When the caching option is enabled, it creates a folder (in the specified path) with the name of currently loaded model.
3. Files in that folder represent different context caches. Koboldcpp reads their names and put them in the initial contexts list (to give to Lite later).
4. The server tracks the currently used context name. Initially it is "(default)".
5. When receiving a generation request it checks the file with the name of chosen cache file:
- If there is no file yet, we start generation as usual;
- If it is equal to the current used cache, we still process as usual;
- But if the file exists and is different from the requested, koboldcpp ditches the current context and reads that file, importing it.
6. After the generation is finished, koboldcpp always saves the current context to the cache file, even in case of aborted input.
7. Example: `--contextcache "C:/koboldcpp/cache/"` may produce:
- `C:/koboldcpp/cache/pygmalion-2-13b.Q5_K_M/(default).cache`
- `C:/koboldcpp/cache/pygmalion-2-13b.Q5_K_M/Story 1.cache`
- `C:/koboldcpp/cache/Lexi-Llama-3-8B-Uncensored-Q5_K_M/(default).cache`
- `C:/koboldcpp/cache/Mistral-Large-Instruct-2407-Q4_K_S/mytest.cache`
- `C:/koboldcpp/cache/Mistral-Large-Instruct-2407-Q4_K_S/second_tab.cache`
- `C:/koboldcpp/cache/Mistral-Large-Instruct-2407-Q4_K_S/Проверка.cache`
(Default file wouldn't be generated if all requests were using already customized names)
8. Cache files won't be deleted automatically, even when becoming orphaned, with the base model not used anymore. That's why we're asking user for the path, and not using any implicit one.

Considerations:
- What about drafting? In the best case, this should work flawlessly for storing context of draft model, maybe by saving draft cache in a subfolder (with the drafter name).
- Safety of filenames? Koboldcpp must reasonably validate user supplied cache names (to disallow special characters), and refuse to use a bad name, throwing a generation error without any fallback (so the user clearly sees the problem instead of thinking that caching works when it does not).
- File format? Does llama.cpp have a well-established binary format for context cache? Would it be possible to use it as is, inferring everything else from the currently loaded model, assuming the cache file was not tampered or swapped between versions?
- Print to console a warning stating that while context caching is enabled, the server will be vulnerable to deny of service if a malicious user would request infinitely many new contexts, filling the disk space.

How is that sound?
There are three major use cases when this feature will really help:
1. When the model is so slow in reprocessing but your story is large, and you want to reboot the system without having to wait a lot of time to continue later.
2. When the model is so large that you can't run two or more instances of it at the same time to play a different story in each one (agents, characters, testing system prompts, etc.)
3. When the drafting is working well but takes all VRAM, so you cannot reasonably run any other model side to it in another instance, so the only way to ask something unrelated to the main story is to destroy the context and then wait for reprocessing.

Everything comes down to how quick the cache swap would be. I imagine using fast NVMe for cache folder (and having some RAM free for filesystem needs, so recently accessed files won't load entirely from disk) would greatly speed up everything, comparing to "just reprocess the history on each different requested story" that we have currently.

candidates.title: Flatpak Support
candidates.body:
Summary: Package Koboldcpp as a Flatpak application and publish it to Flathub for easy installation and distribution.

Motivation: Improve accessibility and ease of use by making Koboldcpp available through Flathub, allowing users to install it with a single command and benefit from Flatpak's sandboxing and updates system.

Proposed Solution:
• Create a Flatpak manifest and build Koboldcpp as a Flatpak app.
• Publish the app to Flathub for public access.

Priority: Very low until flatpak supports GPU's properly. (OP had this as high)

Benefits: Easier installation, better security through sandboxing, automatic updates, and broader user adoption.

candidates.title: Is Pascal CUDA compatibility broken from versions 1.79.1 onwards? (ERROR: CUDA kernel mul_mat_vec has no device code compatible with CUDA arch 520.)
candidates.body:
`ERROR: CUDA kernel mul_mat_vec has no device code compatible with CUDA arch 520. ggml-cuda.cu was compiled for: __CUDA_ARCH_LIST__`


Recently I've been trying to use my Quadro GP100 which is a Pascal graphics card for KoBoldCpp use, until I happened to encounter such error prompts.

Personally I think there's nothing to do with either the graphics drivers or the CUDA toolkits, for I already have CUDA versions 10.2, 11.7, 11.8, 12.1, 12.4 and the driver supporting CUDA 12.4 installed.

Furthermore, I've been running on another CUDA graphics card of Turing generation in the same machine with the Pascal one running together, completely on GPU itself on KoBoldCpp versions 1.60.1 and (cuda12.exe) 1.79.1 through the current 1.83, all of which seem without any issues. And I'm currently still running it through another KoBoldCpp instance.

So I am wondering, if there's something that breaks the compatibility with Pascal CUDA GPUs since version 1.79.1 onwards, for I've been tested versions 1.79.1, 1.81.1, 1.82.4, 1.83, all of which just throw out the same error of incompatibility.

Even though it is okay for me since I've been checking through all versions from 1.63 up to 1.78 to work fine on the Pascal graphics, I guess it would be my Pascal graphics' goodbye to the concurrent Deepseek models, since these did fail on my Turing graphics until I went here and checked out the latest version that time claiming to support for them.


--- Additional information ---

Operating system: Windows 10 21H2, without guests or VMs over it (Hyper-V also disabled) as the error still persists.

candidates.title: Different tokenization leads to BLAS reprocessing
candidates.body:
Since different token sequences may form the same printed text, there is a chance that whatever the model outputs would not tokenize back to the same exact tokens when used as an input in the following turn.

The drawback is that some part of yellow text might be reprocessed again the next time, as if the user made an edition somewhere, because context cache would miss due to token id discrepancy.

Here is an example with quantized DeepSeek R1 (I could not see it on distilled model, probably because of a different tokenizer vocabulary):

`<｜User｜>Repeat the string: "**Duration:** Around ~2-4 days."<｜end▁of▁sentence｜><｜Assistant｜><think></think>**Duration`

The model (at zero temp) writes:
`:** Around ~2-4 days.<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>`

Thing is, its `":**"` is one token (weird but okay), then `" ~"` (space+tilde), then `"2"` and so on.
But! This string in input is processed as `":**"`, then `" "` (space), then `"~"` (just tilde), and `"2"`. One token more.

So, if you add nothing and just hit "Generate more" – you will see 7 tokens as a new prompt (or whatever the length of the rest of the generated text), instead of just 1 token to process.
This works only the first time, because reprocessing "fixes" the cache, making the model believe it wrote `" "`+`"~"` rather than `" ~"`.

I think it is possible to fix this by pretending that user's input was tokenized just as current context as long as their text representation is the same. Here is my general idea in pseudocode (in javascript; I know you have C++ there, it is just easier for me to show JS):

```js
function find_matching_prefix_length (context_tokens, input_tokens) {
  i = 0; // valid matching index in context_tokens
  j = 0; // valid matching index in input_tokens
  while (i<context_tokens.length && j<input_tokens.length) { // ensure bound
    if (context_tokens[i]==input_tokens[j]) { // token is the same
      i++;
      j++;
      continue; // increment both and continue
    }
    // tokens don't match but may refer to the same text
    a = ""; // part of next context
    b = ""; // part of next input
    x = i; // copy of indices, because we need to preserve valid values
    y = j;
    while (true) { // trying to fit tokens together
      if (x==context_tokens.length || y==input_tokens.length) { // hit the end of either array
        return [i,j]; // return last known valid indices
      }
      a = a + token_to_string(context_tokens[x]); // concatenate next converted text to accumulate prefix
      b = b + token_to_string(input_tokens[y]);
      s = min(a.length, b.length); // common length to compare
      if (a.substring(0,s)!=b.substring(0,s)) { // if texts are different, we stop
        return [i,j]; // returning last valid
      }
      if (a.length==b.length) { // discrepancy resolved, continue scanning forward
        i = x+1; // set new valid indices for the outer loop
        j = y+1;
        break;
      }
      if (a.length<b.length) { // add one token of context since it is shorter
        x++;
      } else { // add one token of input when it was shorter
        y++;
      }
    }
  }
  return [i, j]; // matched till the end
}
```

Basically, when you see different tokens, try to resolve: render those tokes to strings; their length may be different, so we compare only the common prefix. If that wrong – then we cannot resolve: prompt is not equal to context; otherwise, we have a change that the next token would "fill the gap". Append the next token as text to whichever string was shorter and compare again. We'll either end up with equal length and content (meaning the discrepancy is resolved), or hit the different text / end of either array. The algorithm eats even different tokens with the same exact text (it would enter the inner loop, just compare and break back).

Then, you would have "how many tokens of context are valid no matter what were the input tokens" and "how many of input tokens to strip to get the actual continuation of the user prompt with respect to the existing context".

I believe that preserving exact output tokens in the context is important, because a different tokenization may in theory affect logprobs later, but the model at zero temperature should continue printing whatever it was trying to say no matter if the previous generation aborted or not.

(Fairly enough, you can say "but if you paste the same history to a new story it won't anymore, because the tokenization already rendered differently everywhere", but I still think that a history restart is not as frequent as mere Abort that should not change the meaning of existing text!)

And of course, unnecessary reprocessing is bad by itself.

candidates.title: DRY sampling is broken in release version 1.73
candidates.body:
I was wondering why I was suddenly getting a lot of repeating phrases again so I turned up the DRY multiplier and still the phrases would repeat so I suspected something is wrong with the backend and seems I was right. Using --debugmode you can see the DRY penalties are reported in the console but not properly applied.

Here's a part where the model is trying to repeat the clichéd phrase "her red eyes sparkling with mischief."
With DRY penalty off (multiplier 0) this is what I get:
![iblHL](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77167df2-da01-44a6-9acf-cf55d25ef427)
Now with DRY multiplier at 0.1 on koboldcpp 1.72 it penalizes some tokens, most notably the token "red" and this is what happens:
![DvpjZ](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/921b4fea-400d-4a82-9d65-aeaa4b171ae7)
Using 0.8 multiplier the penalty is so big "red" is gone completely.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6f33cdd-891e-4a77-ab32-97546a0d32d6)

Now let's try koboldcpp 1.73
DRY multiplier 0.1:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/432e8b88-b065-409a-a7e8-08d63d4caa36)
DRY multiplier 0.8:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4353780-39e7-444d-ae50-729dbc907d7d)
As you can see DRY tries to desperately penalize these tokens, each one more than the last because the penalized string keeps continuing but the probabilities don't reflect the penalty.

**Additional Information:**
Temperature 0.5, every other sampler disabled.
launch params used: `.\koboldcpp.exe --usecublas --threads 5 --highpriority --nommap --gpulayers 20 --contextsize 16384 --debugmode`
Windows exe releases of 1.72 and 1.73 used (cuda12 version)
Model: mini-magnum-12b-v1.1.Q5_K_M.gguf (Mistral-Nemo finetune)
Windows 10 with Ryzen 3600, RTX 2070 Super (though I don't think these would matter).

candidates.title: ContextShift sometimes degrades output
candidates.body:
I'm trying storywriting with KoboldCpp. At some point the story will get longer than the context and KoboldCpp starts evicting tokens from the beginning, with the (newer) ContextShift feature. Sometimes this degrades the output significantly. It will get into repetition-loops, barely write correct sentences and forget who is doing what. That happens after the KV cache got messed with. The story had been fine for the first 4k tokens (or so, dependant on context size) before.

Does this also happen to other people? I'm not sure if it does this every time. I'm pretty sure it doesn't always happen. Other times it keeps generating high-quality output. I've changed too many settings simultaneously and tried different models, so I can't really pin it down and make a good statement.

I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong or if this is a bug. I have also set RoPE scaling and I regularly edit the last paragraphs before (re)generating more output.

(I really like the speedup with ContextShift, so disabling it won't be an option.)

# Environment and Context

Platform: Linux (Debian), CPU only
KoboldCpp: On branch concedo, commit 0ca814e

```
$ make clean && make LLAMA_OPENBLAS=1 LLAMA_CLBLAST=1
$ python3 koboldcpp.py --threads 2 --contextsize 8192 --port 5001 models/LLaMA2-13B-Psyfighter2.Q4_K_M.gguf
```

# Steps to Reproduce

Not sure. I'd like to hear other people's experiences. Generate long output, past the (initial) context window. Keep generating more and more text.


# Prerequisites

Please answer the following questions for yourself before submitting an issue.

- [x] I am running the latest code. Development is very rapid so there are no tagged versions as of now.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I [searched using keywords relevant to my issue](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/filtering-and-searching-issues-and-pull-requests) to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new bug or useful enhancement to share.
